Last week, Apple launched what could be called its first batch of AI-powered wearables — the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Both products, along with Siri AI, feature a brand-new "Audio Intelligence" capability. However, a Bloomberg report today indicates that another AI product — the long-rumoured wearable pendant — has been shelved.

Apple's AI wearable plans, at least for now, no longer include a pendant product.

The AI era has spawned plenty of software innovation, but it has yet to truly deliver an entirely new category of product.

Of course, some have tried — the now-failed Humane Ai Pin, for example. Meta's AI smart glasses have had some success, but the market remains quite niche.

There were rumours that Apple was developing several AI-centric wearables, and last week's launch of the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 can be considered the first products to materialise.

However, according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple has been working on a wearable pendant equipped with a camera, but it sounds like progress on this product has stalled for now.

Gurman previously reported that the pendant would "serve as an always-on camera for the iPhone, while also featuring a built-in microphone for Siri input."

It now appears that Apple has decided to shelve this project and is focusing on bringing AI to the Apple Watch, while also developing a camera-equipped version of the AirPods and smart glasses set to launch in 2027.

It's currently unclear how AI will be integrated, but Gurman also says Apple is exploring a new screen-less, health-focused wearable in a bid to compete more effectively with WHOOP.

Are you interested in getting your hands on an AI pendant designed by Apple? Let us know in the comments section.
